text: There are only three reasons why things do not happen the way you want them to happen as a leader.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj about leadership and managing teams effectively. Anuj explains his framework for diagnosing performance issues when team members aren't delivering expected results. He breaks down the root causes into three categories: capability gaps (can't do), motivation/alignment problems (won't do), or systemic setup failures (weren't set up to do). This framework helps leaders identify whether they need to coach, realign, or fix organizational processes.
text_ko: 리더로서 일이 원하는 대로 안 되는 이유는 딱 세 가지예요.
text_zh: 作为领导，事情没有按你预期发展，无非就是三个原因。
text_es: Solo hay tres razones por las que las cosas no salen como quieres cuando eres líder.
key_sentence: There are only three reasons why things do not happen the way you want them to happen as a leader.
original_text: There are only three reasons why things do not happen the way you want them to happen as a leader. You can look at a person, and you would say either that person can't do, which is a capability issue, or they won't do, which is a motivation or an alignment issue, or they were not set up to do, which is really your problem that you didn't set up the ways of working now design properly.

text: One of the things that I realized once we started working with the products is that product managers and generally, companies are too engrossed in thinking about... because they are very close to the product.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj about his approach to building user experiences for new users. Anuj explains a common bias that product managers develop - they become so immersed in their product that they assume users share their level of engagement and understanding. He argues this creates a disconnect because most consumers don't think about any single product constantly and need to be approached differently when they first encounter a product.
text_ko: 우리가 제품을 다루기 시작하면서 깨달은 것 중 하나는, 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)들이나 대다수의 회사들이 제품에 너무 밀착해 있어서 결국 제품 자체에만 지나치게 몰두한다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我们开始做产品之后我发现一个问题，就是产品经理，还有公司整体，都太钻牛角尖了...因为他们跟产品贴得太近了。
text_es: Una de las cosas que me di cuenta cuando empezamos a trabajar con los productos es que los product managers y en general, las empresas están demasiado metidas pensando en... porque están muy pegados al producto.
key_sentence: Companies are too engrossed in their product, missing broader perspectives.
original_text: One of the things that I realized once we started working with the products is that product managers and generally, companies are too engrossed in thinking about... because they are very close to the product. It's close to their heart, and they're looking at it all the time. They're looking at a lot of minor nuances in terms of how this works and feels, and almost inherent into this is the bias that everybody is thinking about this product all day, all the time, and so on, and so forth.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and feature definition of a product or product line.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers play a crucial role in bridging the gap between engineering, marketing, and customer needs to ensure successful product development.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'product managers' implies a leadership role that requires both technical knowledge and strong interpersonal skills; it is not interchangeable with roles focused solely on engineering or marketing.

text: There's very interesting insight that I heard from Scott Belsky from Adobe, and then now, he's doing very interesting stuff, and that stayed with me which was you have to think about users on modern internet consumers having three attributes.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Anuj continues explaining his philosophy for designing products for new users. He shares a framework from Adobe's Scott Belsky that characterizes internet users with three key traits. According to this framework, users are 'lazy' (don't want to spend time learning), 'vain' (resistant to changing existing habits), and 'selfish' (need clear personal benefits). This insight helps product managers design onboarding experiences that account for user reluctance and skepticism.
text_ko: 어도비의 스콧 벨스키(Scott Belsky)에게서 들은 진짜 흥미로운 인사이트가 하나 있어요. 지금도 그가 하는 일이 흥미로운데, 그 말이 오래 남더라고요 — 현대 인터넷 사용자(modern internet consumers)를 생각할 때는 그들이 세 가지 속성을 가지고 있다고 봐야 한다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我听Adobe的Scott Belsky说过一个特别有意思的观点，他现在做的事情也很有意思，这个观点一直让我印象深刻，就是说现在互联网用户有三个特点，你必须要考虑到。
text_es: Hay una reflexión muy interesante que escuché de Scott Belsky de Adobe, que ahora está haciendo cosas muy interesantes, y que se me quedó grabada: tienes que pensar que los usuarios de internet hoy en día tienen tres características.
key_sentence: Modern internet consumers are lazy, vain, and selfish, which stayed with me.
original_text: There's very interesting insight that I heard from Scott Belsky from Adobe, and then now, he's doing very interesting stuff, and that stayed with me which was you have to think about users on modern internet consumers having three attributes. So they are lazy, they are vain, and they're selfish.

vocabulary.definition: A deep understanding of a complex situation or problem, often leading to new perspectives or solutions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, insights are crucial for making informed decisions, driving innovation, and understanding customer behavior.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'insight' implies a valuable understanding, it is often used to suggest a revelation that can significantly impact strategy or operations.

vocabulary.definition: Characteristics or qualities that define or describe an individual, object, or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, attributes are often used to analyze products, customer segments, or employee skills to enhance decision-making and strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'attributes' can imply both inherent qualities and those that can be developed or influenced over time.

text: We are product managers, and we are in the business of influence. Users are doing something, and now we want them to do something else. Our engineers are doing something, and now we want to influence them into building something fast.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj about effective messaging and value propositions for users. Anuj reframes the entire role of product management as fundamentally being about influence - not just influencing users to adopt products, but also influencing engineers to build features quickly and leadership to approve plans. He argues that viewing product management through this lens of influence helps PMs think more strategically about how they approach all their relationships.
text_ko: 우리는 제품 관리자(product managers)예요. 우리의 일은 영향력을 행사하는 거예요. 사용자(users)들은 지금 어떤 행동을 하고 있는데, 우리가 원하는 건 그들이 다른 행동을 하도록 만드는 거예요. 엔지니어(engineers)들도 지금 뭔가 하고 있고, 우리는 그들이 무언가를 빠르게 만들어 내도록 설득하고 싶어요.
text_zh: 我们是产品经理，干的就是影响别人的活儿。用户现在在做这个，我们想让他们去做那个。工程师现在在搞这个，我们得想办法让他们快点把我们要的东西做出来。
text_es: Somos product managers, y nuestro trabajo es influir. Los usuarios están haciendo algo, y ahora queremos que hagan otra cosa. Nuestros desarrolladores están trabajando en algo, y ahora necesitamos convencerlos de que construyan algo rápido.
key_sentence: We are in the business of influence, wanting users and engineers to sign off.
original_text: We are product managers, and we are in the business of influence. Users are doing something, and now we want them to do something else. Our engineers are doing something, and now we want to influence them into building something fast. Really, leadership has some plans. We'll influence them to, essentially, look at a plan, and basically, sign off, and do something else. We are in the business of influence, and you are doing this all the time internally.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, influence often refers to the ability of product managers to sway user behavior or engineer decisions to align with strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While influence can imply persuasion, it often carries a connotation of subtlety rather than overt coercion.

text: The other part that I found interesting here is that I really truly believe in the power of three. So I actually ask my teams to write three press releases, alternative and divergent like, 'What if we...' Suppose you're launching a membership program.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks about how Anuj operationalizes the 'working backwards' process from Amazon's playbook. Beyond writing a single press release, Anuj explains his approach of creating three divergent press releases for any major product decision. Each press release explores a fundamentally different strategic direction - for example, when launching a membership program, one might explore different tier structures while another might explore a completely different approach like points-based pricing.
text_ko: 여기서 제가 흥미롭게 본 또 다른 점은 제가 정말로 '세의 힘(power of three)'을 믿는다는 거예요. 그래서 저는 팀들에게 실제로 세 개의 보도자료(press releases)를 쓰라고 요청해요 — 대안적이고 각기 다른 방식으로, '만약 우리가…'라고 시작하는 식으로요. 예를 들어 멤버십 프로그램(membership program)을 출시한다고 가정해보세요.
text_zh: 还有一点我觉得挺有意思的，就是我特别相信"三选一"的力量。所以我会让团队写三份新闻稿，每份都不一样，都是"要是我们这样做会怎样..."的思路。比如说你要推出会员项目吧。
text_es: La otra cosa que me parece súper interesante es que yo de verdad creo en el poder del tres. Entonces les pido a mis equipos que escriban tres comunicados de prensa, pero alternativas bien diferentes, como "¿Y si...?" Digamos que vas a lanzar un programa de membresías.
key_sentence: I believe in the power of three; ask teams for alternative and divergent ideas.
original_text: The other part that I found interesting here is that I really truly believe in the power of three. So I actually ask my teams to write three press releases, alternative and divergent like, 'What if we...' Suppose you're launching a membership program. So, instead of two tiers, let's do three tiers, or for example, let's take another one which is instead of building a membership, let's build up tiering pricing program with membership points.

vocabulary.definition: Describing ideas, paths, or approaches that are different or varied from a common point or standard.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, divergent thinking is encouraged during brainstorming sessions to foster creativity and innovation by exploring multiple perspectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While divergent can imply a positive exploration of alternatives, it may also suggest a lack of focus if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: A structured initiative that offers exclusive benefits or services to individuals who pay a fee or meet specific criteria to join.
vocabulary.businessContext: Membership programs are commonly used in businesses to build customer loyalty, enhance engagement, and generate recurring revenue through subscription models.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a sense of community and belonging, which can enhance customer retention and satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: An official statement issued to media outlets to announce news or developments related to an organization, product, or event.
vocabulary.businessContext: Press releases are a key tool in public relations and marketing, used to communicate important information and generate media coverage for a company.
vocabulary.nuance: While press releases are formal communications, they should be crafted to engage the audience and convey the significance of the news effectively.

text: Unless you really... and I'm not saying you need to be an authority of that.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks about Anuj's philosophy that product managers should be more 'full-stack' than most currently are. Anuj explains that successful PMs must either develop deep expertise across multiple disciplines (marketing, engineering, business) or build strong partnerships with experts in those areas. He emphasizes that PMs can't succeed by focusing only on their narrow product area - they need to understand and influence the full ecosystem that makes products successful.
text_ko: 정말 그렇지 않은 이상... 그리고 제가 말하는 건 그 분야의 권위자가 될 필요는 없다는 거예요.
text_zh: 除非你真的...我不是说你一定要成为这方面的专家。
text_es: A menos que realmente... y no digo que tengas que ser un experto en eso.
key_sentence: Unless you really... and I'm not saying you need to be an authority of that.
original_text: Unless you really... and I'm not saying you need to be an authority of that. Either you are very, very good at that, or you have built partnerships, and have run your ideas or product through those people and gotten weighted from them, and finally made a decision around that part, I don't think you'll be very successful.

vocabulary.definition: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience. It can also refer to a person or organization having control or influence in a specific area.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, authority often pertains to leadership roles where individuals are responsible for guiding teams and making strategic decisions. It can also refer to subject matter experts whose opinions are highly regarded in their fields.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'authority' implies a level of respect and recognition, it can also suggest a hierarchical structure that may not always be welcomed in collaborative environments.

text: So we essentially saw that if a startup actually usually wants to do a bunch of things across the border, there's always like, 'Hey, I should be investing in tech debt or building core platforms. That would really help my product in the long term.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj to explain his 'four BB framework' for product strategy. Anuj describes how startups typically face competing priorities across different types of work. He explains that engineering teams often push for technical infrastructure improvements and paying down tech debt, arguing these investments will benefit products long-term, while product managers want to focus on feature development and user-facing improvements. This tension creates the need for a strategic framework to allocate resources.
text_ko: 그래서 우리가 본 바로는, 스타트업들은 보통 여러 영역에서 이것저것 하려고 하는데, 늘 "기술 부채(tech debt)에 투자하거나 핵심 플랫폼(core platforms)을 구축해야 해요. 그게 장기적으로 우리 제품에 정말 도움이 될 거예요"라고 생각하더라고요.
text_zh: 我们基本上发现，如果一个初创公司想要跨界做很多事情，总会有这种想法：'我应该投入一些技术债务(tech debt)或者搭建核心平台，这样长远来看对我的产品会很有帮助。'
text_es: Básicamente lo que vimos es que si una startup quiere hacer muchas cosas a la vez, siempre surge el tema de "Oye, debería estar invirtiendo en deuda técnica (tech debt) o construyendo plataformas base. Eso realmente me ayudaría con mi producto a largo plazo."
key_sentence: if a startup actually usually wants to do a bunch of things across the border
original_text: So we essentially saw that if a startup actually usually wants to do a bunch of things across the border, there's always like, 'Hey, I should be investing in tech debt or building core platforms. That would really help my product in the long term. That's super important,' and that's my engineering managers and largely, people asking for that bandwidth.

vocabulary.definition: The act of allocating resources, usually money, with the expectation of generating an income or profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, investing often refers to funding projects, technologies, or assets that are expected to yield future returns.
vocabulary.nuance: While investing typically implies a financial commitment, it can also encompass time and effort directed towards growth opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Fundamental systems or technologies that serve as the backbone for applications or services within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, core platforms are essential for developing products and ensuring scalability, reliability, and integration with other services.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a foundational importance, indicating that these platforms are critical for operational success and should be prioritized in development.

vocabulary.definition: A time frame that extends into the future, typically beyond one year, focusing on sustainability and enduring outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, long-term considerations are crucial for planning investments, growth trajectories, and overall vision.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a broader perspective, emphasizing the importance of patience and foresight in achieving lasting success.
